title: Eastern US lilac bloom records had fewer weekend dates than the calendar reference in 1965-1986
abstract: We tested whether recorded first-bloom dates were more common on weekends in four US lilac samples from 1965 to 2008. We used 9,015 records from repeated plants. The eastern 1965-1986 sample had 25.94% weekend dates, below the 28.57% reference. The departure was -2.63 percentage points, with a four-test adjusted state-and-year cluster interval of -4.39 to -0.87. A yearly weekday-phase test gave an adjusted p-value of 0.0122. Flag removal, equal plant weights, and state omissions kept this deficit. Three other region-period intervals included zero. This is a calendar pattern in recorded dates. It does not establish a reporting delay, a change over time, or a climate or pollution effect. Unknown visits, different plant types, selected long records, finite seasonal windows, and model assumptions limit inference. The package includes a raw-data build, source hashes, the eligible panel, all results, code, a figure, and independent date and count checks.

display.caption: Weekend departure from 2/7 and weekday shares in four region-period samples. Intervals use state and year clusters and a four-test correction.

citations.reason: We adapt its public raw source and sample selection for a new calendar test. Records overlap.
